## Early life and education
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]
Han Kang was born on 27 November 1970 in [Gwangju](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangju "Gwangju"), South Korea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:0-4) According to her father, she is named for the [Han River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_River_\(Korea\) "Han River \(Korea\)") ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 한강; [RR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean"): _Hangang_).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-5) Her family is noted for its literary background. Her father is novelist [Han Seung-won](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Seung-won "Han Seung-won"). They made history as the first father and daughter to both be awarded the [Yi Sang Literary Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Sang_Literary_Award "Yi Sang Literary Award").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-6) Her older brother, Han Dong-rim, is also a novelist, while her younger brother, Han Kang-in, is a novelist and cartoonist.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:0-4)
At the age of nine, Han moved to [Suyu-ri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suyu-dong "Suyu-dong") in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), when her father quit his teaching job to become a full-time writer, four months before the [Gwangju Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangju_Uprising "Gwangju Uprising"), a pro-democracy movement that ended in the military's massacre of students and civilians. She first learned about the massacre when she was 12, after discovering at home a secretly circulated memorial album of photographs taken by a German journalist, [Jürgen Hinzpeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Hinzpeter "Jürgen Hinzpeter").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-7) This discovery deeply influenced her view on humanity and her literary works.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-litencyc-1)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-8)
